questions.scenario: Your parents just installed a new high-speed Wi-Fi router at home, but they put a strict password on it.

options.A: I try to guess their password or find a backdoor to connect my phone without them knowing.
options.B: I check the router's log history to figure out exactly what time the connection goes off every night.
options.C: I suggest setting up a hidden 'Guest Network' so our neighbors don't use up all our data.
options.D: I take charge of the password and set a strict house rule on who gets to use the Wi-Fi during exam season.

questions.scenario: A suspicious forward arrives on the family WhatsApp group claiming 'Get Free 5G Recharge by clicking here!'.

options.A: I use an incognito tab to click the link just to see exactly how they are trying to trick people.
options.B: I closely examine the fake URL spelling and trace where the fake website was actually created.
options.C: I change the family group settings so only admins can post, completely blocking future spam.
options.D: I send a stern voice note warning all the uncles and aunts about OTP fraud and tell them to delete the message.

questions.scenario: Your younger sibling keeps trying to unlock your smartphone to play games when you are not looking.

options.A: I purposefully leave it unlocked with a fake game open, just to catch them red-handed.
options.B: I check my screen time and battery usage history to prove exactly which games they played while I was asleep.
options.C: I create a super complex multi-layer lock: Face ID, a tough password, and a hidden secure folder for my personal apps.
options.D: I confiscate their tablet and negotiate: 'You get 30 minutes of game time only if you finish your homework first.'

questions.scenario: The shared family laptop gets infected with a weird virus, and everything becomes extremely slow.

options.A: I boot the laptop in safe mode and aggressively try to hunt down and delete the virus files manually.
options.B: I dig deep into the browser history to find out exactly which sketchy movie download site caused the infection.
options.C: I completely wipe the laptop, reinstall Windows, and set up a solid antivirus with a proper automatic backup drive.
options.D: I scold whoever downloaded the virus and enforce a strict new rule: 'Nobody downloads anything without asking me.'

questions.scenario: You get a scam call from someone pretending to be a bank manager, asking for an OTP.

options.A: I play along, give them fake numbers, and waste as much of their time as possible for fun.
options.B: I note down their number, check Truecaller, and listen to the background noise to figure out where they are calling from.
options.C: I immediately install a strong spam-call blocker on all my parents' phones so these calls never ring again.
options.D: I disconnect immediately, block the number, and lecture my parents on the latest 'Jamtara' style scams.

questions.scenario: You have a secret folder of embarrassing old photos or a personal diary on your computer.

options.A: I hide it in a brilliant, unexpected place and challenge my friends to see if they can find it.
options.B: I leave a tiny, invisible trap (like a piece of paper on the keyboard) to prove if someone snooped while I was away.
options.C: I hide the photos inside three nested invisible folders with boring names like 'Class 9 Geography Notes'.
options.D: I openly declare to everyone in the house that anyone touching my laptop will face severe consequences.

questions.scenario: The school computer lab IT teacher has strictly blocked YouTube and all gaming websites.

options.A: I quietly figure out a proxy server or a VPN extension to easily bypass the school's firewall.
options.B: I open the browser's developer tools to see exactly how the IT teacher managed to block the websites.
options.C: I mentally design a much smarter network system that would successfully block even the proxy sites.
options.D: I go talk to the Principal to officially request unblocking educational YouTube channels for our science project.

questions.scenario: You are playing a multiplayer mobile game (like BGMI or Free Fire) and an opponent is clearly hacking/cheating.

options.A: I try to find a glitch or an exploit in the map to outsmart them and beat them at their own game.
options.B: I record the gameplay and analyze how their 'aimbot' works to figure out exactly what cheat they bought.
options.C: I think about how the game developers could change the server code to permanently block this specific cheat.
options.D: I immediately report the player, warn my squad over the mic, and coordinate a safe exit from the match.

questions.scenario: Your parents ask you to manage the family's shared Netflix or Amazon Prime Video account.

options.A: I try to guess my friends' passwords so I can get free access to other OTT platforms too.
options.B: I check the viewing history to find out exactly who has been messing up my movie recommendations.
options.C: I set up individual profiles with PIN locks and strict age-control settings for the younger cousins.
options.D: I monitor how many screens are active and kick out distant relatives who are using it without permission.

questions.scenario: When dealing with technology, what is your ultimate motivation?

options.A: I love breaking the rules, finding hidden loopholes, and outsmarting the system.
options.B: I love solving mysteries, digging into the data, and finding out exactly what went wrong.
options.C: I love building strong, unbreakable structures and organizing things perfectly so they never fail.
options.D: I love being the leader, making the rules, and protecting my people from digital threats.

Ethical_Hacker.title: Ethical Hacker / Red Teamer
Ethical_Hacker.primary_match_text: The System Breaker! You have a curious, rebellious mind. You love finding loopholes, bypassing rules, and thinking exactly like a hacker to expose weaknesses.
Ethical_Hacker.day_in_the_life: Being legally paid to hack into corporate systems! You act as the 'attacker' (Red Team) to find security flaws in apps and websites before real criminals can exploit them.
Ethical_Hacker.alternative_match_text: Penetration Tester, Vulnerability Assessor, Bug Bounty Hunter
Ethical_Hacker.roadmap: 11th/12th (Science/PCM) -> B.Tech in Computer Science (CSE) -> Earn global certifications like CEH (Certified Ethical Hacker) or OSCP. Participate in Bug Bounty programs.

Malware_Analyst.title: Malware Analyst / Digital Forensics
Malware_Analyst.primary_match_text: The Cyber Detective! You are highly analytical and love solving mysteries. When a cyber attack happens, you dig into the evidence to find the truth.
Malware_Analyst.day_in_the_life: Working like a crime scene investigator for computers. You reverse-engineer dangerous viruses, analyze hacking logs, and track down exactly how cybercriminals stole the data.
Malware_Analyst.alternative_match_text: Incident Responder, Threat Intelligence Analyst, Security Researcher
Malware_Analyst.roadmap: 11th/12th (Science/PCM) -> B.Tech in IT or Computer Science -> Master's in Cyber Security -> Certifications like CHFI (Computer Hacking Forensic Investigator).

Security_Architect.title: Security Architect
Security_Architect.primary_match_text: The Digital Fortress Builder! You are creative but highly organized. You love designing complex, unbreakable systems to keep the bad guys out.
Security_Architect.day_in_the_life: Designing the ultimate defense system for banks or tech giants. You set up complex firewalls, create secure network structures, and ensure hackers cannot breach the company's servers.
Security_Architect.alternative_match_text: Network Security Engineer, Cloud Security Architect, Cryptographer
Security_Architect.roadmap: 11th/12th (Science/PCM) -> B.Tech CSE -> Gain strong knowledge of Networking (CCNA) -> Advanced certifications like CISSP or CompTIA Security+.

Cyber_Defense_Commander.title: Cyber Defense Commander (CISO)
Cyber_Defense_Commander.primary_match_text: The Security Boss! You are a natural leader who loves managing people, creating rules, and handling high-pressure crises to keep everyone safe.
Cyber_Defense_Commander.day_in_the_life: Working as the Chief Information Security Officer (CISO). You manage the entire tech army, create security policies, decide the budget, and lead the response team when a major hack occurs.
Cyber_Defense_Commander.alternative_match_text: Security Operations Center (SOC) Manager, IT Risk Manager, Compliance Director
Cyber_Defense_Commander.roadmap: 11th/12th (Science/PCM) -> B.Tech CSE -> Gain years of experience in IT Security -> MBA in IT Management or Certifications like CISM (Certified Information Security Manager).
